title: Arbitrary field restriction of a groupoid has an open surjective arrow projection
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $(V,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ an absolute groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Let $K/k$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension], put $V_K=\operatorname{Spec}K$, and put $R_K=V_K\times_{V,t}R\times_{s,V}V_K$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. On a test scheme $T$, write a point of $R_K$ as $(u,r,v)$ with $t(r)=q(u)$ and $s(r)=q(v)$, where $q:V_K\to V$ is induced by $k\to K$. The operations $s_K(u,r,v)=v$, $t_K(u,r,v)=u$, $e_K(u)=(u,e(q(u)),u)$, $i_K(u,r,v)=(v,i(r),u)$ and $c_K((u,r,v),(v,r^{\prime},w))=(u,c(r,r^{\prime}),w)$ define an absolute groupoid scheme on $(V_K,R_K)$. The middle projection $p:R_K\to R$ is surjective and open on underlying topological spaces. No finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04LQ (lemma-restrict-groupoid-on-field), dotted arrow in its diagram; restriction groupoid operations are those of Groupoids Tag 02VB (lemma-restrict-groupoid).

proof.text: Construct the displayed operations as scheme morphisms using the universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product]. For identity the three components are $(\mathrm{id}_{V_K},e\circ q,\mathrm{id}_{V_K})$; their compatibility is $teq=seq=q$. For inverse use the two exchanged endpoint projections and $i$ on the arrow component; $ti=s$ and $si=t$ give compatibility. On $D=R_K\times_{s_K,V_K,t_K}R_K$, the two middle-arrow projections $r,r^{\prime}:D\to R$ satisfy $s(r)=q(v)=t(r^{\prime})$, hence induce a map into $R\times_{s,V,t}R$. Compose it with $c$ and take the outer endpoints $u,w$. The identities $tc(r,r^{\prime})=t(r)=q(u)$ and $sc(r,r^{\prime})=s(r^{\prime})=q(w)$ supply the map $c_K:D\to R_K$. The source and target are the endpoint projections. These constructions give exactly the formulas in the statement, on every test scheme, and commute with precomposition.

source.place: Tag 02VB (lemma-restrict-groupoid), expanded omitted verification using the fibre-product universal property and Tag 0231 groupoid axioms.

proof.text: Check the groupoid axioms on an arbitrary test scheme $T$, as required by [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. For $a=(u,r,v)$, identity has both endpoints $u$, and inversion exchanges endpoints. The two unit composites are $(u,c(e(q(u)),r),v)=(u,r,v)$ and $(u,c(r,e(q(v))),v)=(u,r,v)$. The inverse composites are $c_K(i_K(a),a)=(v,c(i(r),r),v)=(v,e(q(v)),v)=e_K(v)$ and $c_K(a,i_K(a))=(u,c(r,i(r)),u)=(u,e(q(u)),u)=e_K(u)$. For three composable triples with middle arrows $r,r^{\prime},r^{\prime\prime}$, both associations retain the same two outer endpoints, while their middle arrows agree by $c(c(r,r^{\prime}),r^{\prime\prime})=c(r,c(r^{\prime},r^{\prime\prime}))$. Source and target of a composite are its last and first endpoints. Thus these operations give a groupoid for every $T$, naturally in $T$, which is precisely an absolute groupoid scheme.

source.place: Tag 02VB (lemma-restrict-groupoid), expanded omitted verification using the fibre-product universal property and Tag 0231 groupoid axioms.

proof.text: Put $B=V_K\times_{q,V,t}R$, with projections to $V_K$ and $b:B\to R$, and give $B$ the map $h=s\circ b:B\to V$. The iterated fibre-product universal property identifies $R_K$ with $B\times_{h,V,q}V_K$: the maps in both directions send $(u,r,v)$ to $((u,r),v)$ and back. They are inverse because all three projections agree, so uniqueness in the universal property applies. Write $a:R_K\to B$ for the projection. Then $p=b\circ a$. Here $b$ is the base change of $q$ along $t$, and $a$ is its base change along $h$. Both $V_K$ and $V$ have exactly one point by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; consequently $q$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 04LQ (lemma-restrict-groupoid-on-field), defining cartesian diagram and first sentence of proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open] with field $k$, scheme $X=V_K$, and base scheme $S=R$ carrying $t:R\to V$. It says that $b:B\to R$ is open. Apply it again with $S=B$ carrying $h:B\to V$; it says that $a:R_K\to B$ is open. The ordering of the two factors is immaterial: the swap maps are inverse by the fibre-product universal property, and an isomorphism induces a homeomorphism since its continuous maps are inverse. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] to the surjective $q$ from step 3, first along $t$ and then along $h$. It gives surjectivity of $b$ and $a$. These two cited statements allow arbitrary schemes over $k$ and arbitrary base changes; neither requires finite type or finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 04LQ (lemma-restrict-groupoid-on-field), proof: use Morphisms Tags 0383 (lemma-scheme-over-field-universally-open) and 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective).

proof.text: For every open subset $O\subseteq R_K$, one has $p(O)=b(a(O))$: first $a(O)$ is open in $B$, then $b(a(O))$ is open in $R$. For every point $r_0\in R$, choose $z\in B$ with $b(z)=r_0$, then $y\in R_K$ with $a(y)=z$. This gives $p(y)=r_0$. Hence $p$ is open and surjective. No part of the construction or the two base-change applications imposed a finiteness condition.
